author: Michael Jackson
text:
ACH Compliance Policy (ACH-001) | 1. Purpose/Summary
This policy establishes Veridian Dynamics' compliance requirements under the Nacha Operating Rules for Automated Clearing House (ACH) transactions, which the platform uses to fund transfers from and to linked consumer bank accounts. It covers originator obligations, return rate thresholds, authorization requirements, and the company's role as a Third-Party Sender under its sponsoring bank relationship.

author: Michael Jackson
text:
ACH Compliance Policy (ACH-001) | 2. Background/Context
Veridian Dynamics originates ACH debits and credits through a sponsoring bank relationship with a federally chartered bank partner, operating as a Third-Party Sender under Nacha rules rather than as a direct ACH Originator. Michael Jackson, Director of Payment Operations, manages the relationship and the associated compliance obligations, which include maintaining ACH return rates within Nacha-mandated thresholds to avoid being classified as a High-Risk Originator subject to enhanced monitoring by the sponsoring bank. This version 2.2 update reflects revised internal return-rate monitoring thresholds adopted after the sponsoring bank flagged rising unauthorized-return rates in late 2025 tied to a subset of fraudulent account-linking attempts.

author: Michael Jackson
text:
ACH Compliance Policy (ACH-001) | 3.1 Return Rate Monitoring
Nacha rules require the overall ACH debit return rate to remain below 15%, the administrative return rate below 3%, and the unauthorized return rate below 0.5%, measured on a rolling 60-day basis. Veridian Dynamics maintains an internal early-warning threshold set more conservatively at 0.35% for unauthorized returns to trigger proactive review before approaching the Nacha limit.

author: Michael Jackson
text:
ACH Compliance Policy (ACH-001) | 3.2 Authorization Requirements
All ACH debit authorizations from linked consumer bank accounts are obtained through a micro-deposit or instant account verification process at account linking, with authorization records retained for 2 years following account closure, consistent with Nacha recordkeeping requirements.

author: Michael Jackson
text:
ACH Compliance Policy (ACH-001) | 3.3 Monitoring and Escalation
Payment Operations reviews return rate metrics daily, with any originator entity (the specific internal processing queue used for a given transaction type) approaching 80% of any Nacha threshold escalated to the sponsoring bank's risk team and to the Fraud Risk Committee for review.

author: Michael Jackson
text:
ACH Compliance Policy (ACH-001) | 3.4 Sponsoring Bank Relationship
The sponsoring bank conducts an annual Third-Party Sender risk assessment, reviewing Veridian Dynamics' origination volume, return rate history, and internal controls. The most recent assessment, completed in January 2025, resulted in no findings and reaffirmed the existing origination limits.

author: Michael Jackson
text:
ACH Compliance Policy (ACH-001) | 4. Key Details
Metric: Overall debit return rate | Nacha Threshold: < 15%; Internal Early-Warning Threshold: 10%
Metric: Administrative return rate | Nacha Threshold: < 3%; Internal Early-Warning Threshold: 2%
Metric: Unauthorized return rate | Nacha Threshold: < 0.5%; Internal Early-Warning Threshold: 0.35%
Metric: Authorization record retention | Nacha Threshold: 2 years post-closure; Internal Early-Warning Threshold: 2 years post-closure
Metric: Sponsoring bank risk assessment cadence | Nacha Threshold: Annual; Internal Early-Warning Threshold: Annual

author: Michael Jackson
text:
ACH Compliance Policy (ACH-001) | 5. Exceptions, Risks, or Open Issues
The unauthorized return rate briefly approached the internal 0.35% early-warning threshold in November 2024, reaching 0.31%, prompting the proactive review that led to this policy's revision; the rate has since declined to 0.18% following enhancements to account-linking fraud detection within the broader Fraud Program (FRD-001). Payment Operations continues to monitor for any recurrence tied to the international expansion markets, which use a different account-linking verification flow not yet fully integrated with the domestic return-rate monitoring dashboard; integration is targeted for Q4 2026.

author: Aubrey Graham
text:
AML Program Documentation (AML-001) | 1. Purpose/Summary
This document establishes Veridian Dynamics' Anti-Money Laundering Program, required under the Bank Secrecy Act and applicable state money transmitter regulations. The program defines the four required pillars: a designated AML Compliance Officer, written internal policies and controls, ongoing employee training, and independent testing. It governs suspicious activity monitoring, Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) filing, and currency transaction reporting obligations across the peer-to-peer payment platform.

author: Aubrey Graham
text:
AML Program Documentation (AML-001) | 2. Background/Context
Aubrey Graham serves as the designated AML Compliance Officer, a role distinct from his Sanctions Officer responsibilities described in the Sanctions Program (SAN-001), though both report to the Chief Compliance Officer. The AML Program was substantially expanded in 2023 following the company's growth past 2 million active accounts, which triggered enhanced due diligence expectations under several state regulators' guidance for money transmitters of that scale. This version 3.3 update reflects refinements to the SAR evaluation workflow following a 2025 internal audit that recommended clearer documentation of the monetary thresholds used to trigger manual SAR evaluation, since the prior version described the threshold only in general terms without a specific dollar figure.

author: Aubrey Graham
text:
AML Program Documentation (AML-001) | 3.1 Program Governance
The AML Program operates under the oversight of the Compliance Committee and is independently tested on the same 18-month rotating cycle described in the Compliance Program Documentation (CMP-002). The AML Compliance Officer maintains direct reporting access to the Board Risk Committee for any matter the officer deems to require board-level attention.

section_title: Suspicious Activity Monitoring and SAR Thresholds
author: Aubrey Graham
text:
AML Program Documentation (AML-001) | 3.2 Suspicious Activity Monitoring and SAR Thresholds
Per this program's internal threshold policy, transactions or related transaction patterns aggregating $5,000 or more within a rolling 24-hour period are flagged for manual SAR evaluation by an AML analyst, who determines within 30 days whether the activity warrants a SAR filing. This $5,000 aggregation threshold reflects the regulatory minimum typically applied to money services businesses for SAR evaluation purposes and was formalized in this document following the 2024 audit recommendation.

author: Aubrey Graham
text:
AML Program Documentation (AML-001) | 3.3 Currency Transaction Reporting
Transactions or aggregated related transactions exceeding $10,000 in currency equivalent within a single business day trigger Currency Transaction Report filing obligations, consistent with federal requirements applicable to money services businesses.

author: Aubrey Graham
text:
AML Program Documentation (AML-001) | 3.4 Recordkeeping and Reporting
AML program records, including SAR evaluation documentation regardless of filing decision, are retained for 5 years. Program metrics, including SAR filing volume and average evaluation turnaround time, are reported to the Compliance Committee monthly.

author: Aubrey Graham
text:

author: Aubrey Graham
text:
AML Program Documentation (AML-001) | 5. Exceptions, Risks, or Open Issues
The AML Compliance Officer has noted that the $5,000 manual SAR evaluation threshold formalized in this document should be reflected consistently in the automated alerting configuration maintained by the transaction monitoring system described in the Transaction Monitoring Documentation (TXM-001); a reconciliation review of the actual system-configured alert threshold against this policy threshold is planned but had not been completed as of this document's publication. Additionally, the planned Digital Asset product line (DIG-001) is expected to require new SAR typology guidance specific to digital asset transactions, which has not yet been developed.

author: Noah Kahan
text:
Business Continuity Plan (BCP-001) | 1. Purpose/Summary
This Business Continuity Plan describes how Veridian Dynamics maintains critical business functions during disruptive events, including natural disasters, pandemics, facility loss, and extended technology outages. It covers continuity strategies for people, facilities, vendors, and critical processes, complementing the technical recovery procedures defined in the Disaster Recovery Program (DRP-001). The plan is owned by Operations and overseen by the Enterprise Risk Management function.

author: Noah Kahan
text:
Business Continuity Plan (BCP-001) | 2. Background/Context
The Business Continuity Plan was last substantially revised in 2023 following lessons learned from a regional weather event that disrupted the Gotham City headquarters for four days in late 2022, during which the company relied on an ad hoc remote-work arrangement that was not formally documented anywhere. Noah Kahan, Head of Enterprise Risk Management, led the subsequent formalization effort, establishing designated alternate work arrangements, a crisis management team structure, and defined recovery objectives for critical business processes. This version 3.2 update reflects the addition of the three new international markets entered in Q2 2026 to the plan's geographic scope and a refreshed business impact analysis conducted in April 2026.

author: Noah Kahan
text:
Business Continuity Plan (BCP-001) | 3.1 Business Impact Analysis
The April 2026 business impact analysis identified 11 critical business processes, including transaction processing, customer support, and regulatory reporting, and assigned each a maximum tolerable downtime based on financial, regulatory, and reputational impact of disruption.

author: Noah Kahan
text:
Business Continuity Plan (BCP-001) | 3.2 Recovery Objectives for Critical Functions
The plan establishes an organization-wide Recovery Time Objective of 4 hours for the transaction processing function, reflecting the business's view of maximum tolerable downtime from a customer and regulatory perspective, and a 2-hour objective for critical regulatory reporting functions such as sanctions and AML alert processing.

author: Noah Kahan
text:
Business Continuity Plan (BCP-001) | 3.3 Crisis Management Structure
A Crisis Management Team, chaired by the COO and including representatives from Operations, IT, Legal & Compliance, Finance, and Customer Success, convenes within 1 hour of a declared crisis event to coordinate response, communications, and recovery prioritization.

author: Noah Kahan
text:
Business Continuity Plan (BCP-001) | 3.4 Alternate Facilities and Remote Work
In the event the Gotham City headquarters becomes unavailable, employees are directed to a documented remote-work continuity procedure, with critical on-site functions (data center liaison staff) relocating to a designated alternate office space maintained under a standing agreement with a regional business continuity services provider.

author: Noah Kahan
text:
Business Continuity Plan (BCP-001) | 4. Key Details
Critical business processes identified: 11
Transaction processing RTO (business view): 4 hours
Regulatory reporting function RTO: 2 hours
Crisis Management Team activation: Within 1 hour of declared crisis
Crisis Management Team chair: Chief Operating Officer
Last business impact analysis: April 2026
Geographic scope: HQ (Gotham City) + 3 new international markets

author: Noah Kahan
text:
Business Continuity Plan (BCP-001) | 5. Exceptions, Risks, or Open Issues
Enterprise Risk Management has flagged that the 4-hour business-side Recovery Time Objective for transaction processing set in this plan is more aggressive than the 8-hour technical Recovery Time Objective validated in the Disaster Recovery Program (DRP-001) following the March 2026 failover test. This gap between business expectation and demonstrated technical capability has been raised to the Board Risk Committee, and IT has been asked to evaluate whether further infrastructure investment could close the gap or whether the business-side objective should be revised to match demonstrated capability. A decision is expected by year-end 2026. Separately, continuity arrangements for the three new international markets are still being finalized with local alternate-facility providers and are not expected to be fully in place until Q1 2027.

author: Kylian Mbappe
text:
Customer Due Diligence Documentation (CDD-001) | 1. Purpose/Summary
This document describes Veridian Dynamics' Customer Due Diligence (CDD) procedures, covering identity verification at onboarding, risk-based customer segmentation, and enhanced due diligence triggers for higher-risk customer profiles. CDD procedures operationalize the identification requirements of the AML Program (AML-001) and are owned by the Customer Identification Program team within Legal & Compliance, led by Kylian Mbappe.

author: Kylian Mbappe
text:
Customer Due Diligence Documentation (CDD-001) | 2. Background/Context
Imani Oduya, Director of Customer Identification, oversees CDD procedures that were substantially upgraded in 2024 to support a risk-based tiering model, replacing a prior one-size-fits-all verification approach that required the same documentation from all customers regardless of risk profile. The upgrade was driven partly by customer experience concerns, since the prior approach created friction for low-risk customers performing small transactions, and partly by regulatory expectations that CDD intensity scale with risk, consistent with guidance applicable to money services businesses. This version 2.5 update reflects refinements to the enhanced due diligence triggers following the 2026 Sanctions Risk Assessment's (SAN-002) identification of elevated cross-border remittance risk.

author: Kylian Mbappe
text:
Customer Due Diligence Documentation (CDD-001) | 3.1 Risk-Based Tiering
Customers are segmented into Standard, Enhanced, and High-Risk tiers at onboarding based on factors including transaction volume expectations, geographic indicators, and occupation where disclosed. Standard tier customers complete basic identity verification (name, address, date of birth, government ID number) matched against a third-party identity verification service.

author: Kylian Mbappe
text:
Customer Due Diligence Documentation (CDD-001) | 3.2 Enhanced Due Diligence Triggers
Customers are escalated to Enhanced tier, requiring additional documentation such as proof of address and source-of-funds attestation, if they engage in cross-border remittance activity, request enhanced verification to access higher transaction limits as described in the Consumer Terms and Conditions (CMP-004), or are identified through transaction monitoring as exhibiting a pattern consistent with money services business activity on a personal account.

author: Kylian Mbappe
text:
Customer Due Diligence Documentation (CDD-001) | 3.3 High-Risk Tier and Periodic Review
High-Risk tier customers, a small population identified through a combination of geographic risk, politically exposed person (PEP) screening, and adverse media screening, undergo a full CDD refresh every 12 months rather than the standard tier's 36-month refresh cycle, and are subject to enhanced transaction monitoring sensitivity settings.

author: Kylian Mbappe
text:
Customer Due Diligence Documentation (CDD-001) | 3.4 Ongoing Monitoring
All customer risk tiers are subject to event-driven re-triggering of due diligence review, such as a significant unexplained change in transaction behavior, regardless of the standard periodic refresh schedule.

author: Kylian Mbappe
text:
Customer Due Diligence Documentation (CDD-001) | 4. Key Details
Tier: Standard | Verification Requirements: Name, address, DOB, government ID match; Periodic Refresh Cycle: 36 months
Tier: Enhanced | Verification Requirements: Standard + proof of address, source of funds; Periodic Refresh Cycle: 24 months
Tier: High-Risk | Verification Requirements: Enhanced + PEP/adverse media screening; Periodic Refresh Cycle: 12 months

author: Kylian Mbappe
text:
Customer Due Diligence Documentation (CDD-001) | 5. Exceptions, Risks, or Open Issues
Following the Sanctions Risk Assessment's (SAN-002) identification of elevated cross-border remittance risk, Legal & Compliance is evaluating whether all cross-border remittance customers should be automatically escalated to High-Risk tier rather than Enhanced tier, which would meaningfully increase the periodic refresh workload; a decision is pending further analysis of the resulting High-Risk population size and associated staffing needs. The identity verification service used for Standard tier customers has also experienced a slight increase in false-rejection rates in the newly launched international markets, attributed to inconsistent government ID format support, which the vendor is working to resolve.

author: Dolly Parton
text:
CFT Program Documentation (CFT-001) | 1. Purpose/Summary
This document describes Veridian Dynamics' Countering the Financing of Terrorism (CFT) Program, which operates alongside the AML Program (AML-001) to detect and prevent the use of the payment platform to fund terrorist activity. The program defines typology-based detection rules, escalation procedures for suspected terrorist financing, and coordination requirements with law enforcement and FinCEN, and is overseen by the same AML Compliance Officer function.

author: Dolly Parton
text:
CFT Program Documentation (CFT-001) | 2. Background/Context
While closely integrated with the broader AML Program, the CFT Program is documented separately to reflect its distinct regulatory basis and the specialized typology library used for terrorist financing detection, which differs meaningfully from typical money-laundering typologies in that transaction amounts involved are often far smaller than traditional money-laundering red flags. Dolly Parton oversees the program and works with a specialized analyst trained specifically in terrorist financing typologies, a role added in 2023 in response to evolving FinCEN guidance encouraging money services businesses to develop CFT-specific detection capability rather than relying solely on general AML monitoring.

author: Dolly Parton
text:
CFT Program Documentation (CFT-001) | 3.1 Typology Library
The CFT typology library includes 22 documented red-flag patterns, covering structuring of small-dollar transactions across multiple accounts, rapid pass-through transaction patterns, and connections to geographic regions or counterparties associated with elevated terrorist financing risk per FinCEN advisories. The library is reviewed and updated semi-annually.

author: Dolly Parton
text:
CFT Program Documentation (CFT-001) | 3.2 Detection and Escalation
Transactions matching CFT typology patterns are flagged regardless of dollar amount, reflecting the recognition that terrorist financing transactions are frequently low-value. Flagged transactions are reviewed by the specialized CFT analyst within 48 hours, with confirmed matches escalated immediately to the AML Compliance Officer and, where appropriate, to FinCEN through the SAR filing process with the terrorist financing box specifically indicated.

author: Dolly Parton
text:
CFT Program Documentation (CFT-001) | 3.3 Law Enforcement Coordination
The AML Compliance Officer maintains a point of contact relationship with the FBI's financial crimes task force and responds to voluntary information requests (314(a) requests) within the regulatory timeframe, currently a 2-week response window from receipt.

author: Dolly Parton
text:
CFT Program Documentation (CFT-001) | 3.4 Training
All AML and Fraud Operations analysts complete a 1-hour CFT-specific awareness module annually, in addition to general AML training, covering updated typology examples and recent FinCEN advisories relevant to the payment services industry.

author: Dolly Parton
text:
CFT Program Documentation (CFT-001) | 4. Key Details
CFT typology patterns documented: 22
Typology library review cadence: Semi-annual
Dollar threshold for CFT typology flagging: None (flagged regardless of amount)
CFT analyst review turnaround: 48 hours
314(a) request response window: 2 weeks
Annual CFT training module length: 1 hour

author: Dolly Parton
text:
CFT Program Documentation (CFT-001) | 5. Exceptions, Risks, or Open Issues
The CFT Program currently relies on a single specialized analyst for typology-matched review, creating a key-person risk that Legal & Compliance has flagged for the 2027 staffing planning cycle, particularly given the 48-hour review SLA that could be jeopardized by analyst absence. A cross-training initiative to build a backup reviewer capability is planned but not yet funded. The program's typology library has not yet been evaluated for applicability to the planned Digital Asset product line (DIG-001), which may introduce distinct terrorist-financing typologies not covered by the current 22 patterns.

author: Patrick Mahomes
text:
Compliance Training Documentation (CMP-001) | 1. Purpose/Summary
This document describes the annual Compliance Training curriculum required for all Veridian Dynamics employees, with enhanced modules for employees in customer-facing or transaction-handling roles. Training covers AML/BSA obligations, sanctions awareness, fraud red flags, consumer protection requirements, and data privacy fundamentals. The program is administered through the ComplianceIQ learning management system and is overseen by the Compliance Training Manager under Legal & Compliance.

author: Patrick Mahomes
text:
Compliance Training Documentation (CMP-001) | 2. Background/Context
Veridian Dynamics introduced mandatory annual compliance training in 2021 in connection with its state money transmitter licensing requirements, which obligate the company to demonstrate an ongoing employee training program as a condition of licensure in most operating states. The curriculum has expanded from a single 1-hour general awareness module to a tiered structure reflecting role-based risk exposure. Patrick Mahomes took over as Compliance Training Manager in mid-2024 and led a redesign of the curriculum content delivered through ComplianceIQ, replacing static slide decks with interactive scenario-based modules following feedback that completion rates were high but post- training assessment scores were not improving year over year. The 2025 refresh also incorporated new content addressing elder financial exploitation typologies following guidance issued by state regulators to money services businesses.

author: Patrick Mahomes
text:
Compliance Training Documentation (CMP-001) | 3.1 Curriculum Structure
All employees complete a 4-hour general compliance module annually, covering AML/BSA basics, sanctions awareness, code of conduct, and data privacy. Employees in Customer Success, Fraud Operations, and Legal & Compliance additionally complete role-specific modules: a 2-hour fraud red-flag module for Fraud Operations, and a 1.5-hour consumer complaint handling module for Customer Success.

author: Patrick Mahomes
text:
Compliance Training Documentation (CMP-001) | 3.2 Delivery and Completion Tracking
All training is delivered through ComplianceIQ, which tracks completion status, quiz scores, and time spent per module. Managers receive automated reminder notifications for direct reports who have not completed training 30 days prior to the annual deadline of January 31.

author: Patrick Mahomes
text:
Compliance Training Documentation (CMP-001) | 3.3 Assessment and Remediation
Each module concludes with a 10-question knowledge check requiring a passing score of 80%. Employees who do not pass on the first attempt are given one retake; a second failure triggers automatic escalation to the employee's manager and HR via PeopleHub for an in-person remediation session with Legal & Compliance.

author: Patrick Mahomes
text:
Compliance Training Documentation (CMP-001) | 3.4 2025 Results and 2026 Changes
The 2025 training cycle achieved a 98% completion rate by the January 31 deadline, with the remaining 2% completing within an approved extension window for employees on leave. Average knowledge-check scores improved from 84% in 2024 to 89% in 2025 following the scenario-based redesign.

author: Patrick Mahomes

Compliance Training Documentation (CMP-001) | 5. Exceptions, Risks, or Open Issues
New hires joining after the January 31 deadline are required to complete training within 30 days of their start date rather than waiting for the next annual cycle; compliance with this new-hire requirement is tracked separately and was not included in the 98% completion figure reported for 2025. Legal & Compliance has identified a gap in training content specific to the planned Digital Asset product line, which is expected to require a new module prior to any production launch. Budget for this module has not yet been approved by Finance.

author: Olivia Rodrigo
text:
Compliance Program Documentation (CMP-002) | 1. Purpose/Summary
This document establishes the overarching Compliance Program for Veridian Dynamics, describing the governance structure, policy framework, and oversight mechanisms through which the company satisfies its regulatory obligations as a licensed money services business. The program encompasses AML/BSA compliance, sanctions compliance, consumer protection, and state money transmitter licensing requirements, and defines the roles of the Chief Compliance Officer, the Compliance Committee, and the Board Risk Committee in overseeing the program.

author: Olivia Rodrigo
text:
Compliance Program Documentation (CMP-002) | 2. Background/Context
Veridian Dynamics operates under money transmitter licenses in 47 states and the District of Columbia, and is subject to oversight from state banking regulators as well as federal obligations under the Bank Secrecy Act. The Compliance Program was established in 2021 under the leadership of the founding Chief Compliance Officer and has been revised three times since, most recently under current CCO Olivia Rodrigo, who assumed the role in late 2024 following a multi-state examination that resulted in several supervisory findings related to program documentation and board reporting cadence. This version 3.1 update incorporates corrective actions committed to in the examination response, including a restructured Compliance Committee with defined voting membership and a quarterly reporting template standardized across all sub-programs, including the Sanctions Program (SAN-001), AML Program (AML-001), and Fraud Program (FRD-001).

author: Olivia Rodrigo
text:
Compliance Program Documentation (CMP-002) | 3.1 Governance Structure
The Compliance Committee, chaired by the CCO, includes voting representatives from Legal & Compliance, Operations, Finance, and IT, and meets monthly. The Committee reviews sub-program metrics, approves policy changes, and escalates material issues to the Board Risk Committee, which meets quarterly.

author: Olivia Rodrigo
text:
Compliance Program Documentation (CMP-002) | 3.2 Policy Framework
The Compliance Program sits above five sub-programs: the AML Program, the CFT Program, the Sanctions Program, the Fraud Program, and the Consumer Compliance framework. Each sub-program maintains its own detailed documentation but reports into the Compliance Program through a standardized quarterly metrics template covering volume, exceptions, and remediation status.

author: Olivia Rodrigo
text:
Compliance Program Documentation (CMP-002) | 3.3 Independent Testing
An independent compliance testing function, staffed by two full-time testers reporting to the CCO but organizationally separate from the first-line compliance teams, conducts risk-based testing of controls across all sub-programs on a rotating 18-month cycle. Findings are tracked to closure in a centralized issues-management system.

author: Olivia Rodrigo
text:
Compliance Program Documentation (CMP-002) | 3.4 Licensing and Examination Management
Legal & Compliance maintains a licensing calendar tracking renewal deadlines across all 47 state licenses plus DC, and coordinates responses to routine and for-cause examinations. The most recent multi-state examination concluded in October 2024 with four findings, three of which have been fully remediated as of this document's publication.

The one remaining open examination finding relates to documentation gaps in historical consumer complaint resolution records predating the current Consumer Complaint Resolution Process (CMP-003); full remediation is targeted for Q1 2026 pending a records digitization project led jointly by Legal & Compliance and IT. The Compliance Committee has also flagged resourcing concerns: the independent testing function's two-person staff is considered thin relative to the expanding sub-program scope, particularly with the planned Digital Asset product line, and a budget request for a third tester has been submitted to Finance for the 2026 planning cycle.

author: Beyonce
text:
Consumer Complaint Resolution Process (CMP-003) | 1. Purpose/Summary
This document defines how Veridian Dynamics receives, categorizes, investigates, and resolves consumer complaints submitted through any channel, including in-app support, email, phone, social media, and regulatory referral. It establishes resolution timelines, escalation criteria, and recordkeeping requirements, and is designed to satisfy both internal service-level expectations and applicable state consumer protection regulations governing money transmitters.

author: Beyonce
text:
Consumer Complaint Resolution Process (CMP-003) | 2. Background/Context
Customer Success handles an average of 9,200 consumer complaints per month across all intake channels, a figure that has grown alongside the platform's user base. Prior to 2023, complaint handling was decentralized across individual support agents without a standardized categorization taxonomy, which made it difficult to identify systemic issues or satisfy regulatory recordkeeping expectations during examinations. Beyonce, Director of Customer Success Operations, led the implementation of a centralized complaint-management module within the customer support platform in 2023, and this version 2.3 update reflects refinements made after a 2024 internal audit recommended tightening resolution timelines for complaints involving potential unauthorized transactions, given their heightened regulatory sensitivity under Regulation E principles applied voluntarily by the company even though it is not a bank.

author: Beyonce
text:
Consumer Complaint Resolution Process (CMP-003) | 3.1 Intake and Categorization
All complaints are logged into the centralized complaint-management module within 1 business hour of receipt, regardless of channel. Complaints are categorized into one of eight standard categories: unauthorized transaction, service quality, fee dispute, account access, fraud-related, discrimination/fair lending, privacy, and other.

author: Beyonce
text:
Consumer Complaint Resolution Process (CMP-003) | 3.2 Resolution Timelines
Standard complaints must receive a substantive response within 10 business days and be resolved within 30 calendar days. Complaints categorized as unauthorized transaction are treated as expedited and must receive an initial response within 2 business days and a final resolution within 10 business days, consistent with voluntary Regulation E-aligned practices.

author: Beyonce
text:
Consumer Complaint Resolution Process (CMP-003) | 3.3 Escalation Criteria
Complaints that allege discrimination or fair lending concerns are automatically escalated to Legal & Compliance regardless of dollar amount. Complaints exceeding $10,000 in disputed funds, or any complaint referred by a state regulator, are escalated to the Director of Customer Success Operations and tracked separately for board reporting purposes.

author: Beyonce
text:

author: Legal Drafting Team
text:
Consumer Terms and Conditions (CMP-004) | 1. Purpose/Summary
This document sets forth the Consumer Terms and Conditions governing use of the Veridian Dynamics peer-to-peer payment platform by individual consumers. It covers account eligibility, fee disclosures, transaction limits, dispute rights, liability limitations, and account closure provisions. These terms are presented to every consumer at account creation and must be affirmatively accepted before a consumer can send or receive funds on the platform.

author: Legal Drafting Team
text:
Consumer Terms and Conditions (CMP-004) | 2. Background/Context
The Consumer Terms and Conditions have been revised five times since the platform's 2019 launch, with this version 5.0 reflecting changes necessary to support international expansion into three new markets in Q2 2025 and to clarify liability provisions following feedback from the Consumer Complaint Resolution Process (CMP-003) team regarding recurring confusion over unauthorized transaction liability. The Legal Drafting Team, working with outside counsel, undertook a comprehensive plain-language rewrite of the liability and dispute sections, which were previously criticized in user feedback surveys as difficult to understand. The revised terms were reviewed by the Compliance Committee and approved by the General Counsel prior to publication.

author: Legal Drafting Team
text:
Consumer Terms and Conditions (CMP-004) | 3.1 Eligibility and Account Types
Consumers must be at least 18 years of age and a resident of a jurisdiction where the platform is licensed to operate. Standard consumer accounts are subject to a $2,500 single-transaction limit and a $10,000 rolling 7-day transaction limit unless the consumer completes enhanced identity verification, which raises the rolling 7-day limit to $25,000.

author: Legal Drafting Team
text:
Consumer Terms and Conditions (CMP-004) | 3.2 Fees
Standard peer-to-peer transfers funded by linked bank account or platform balance are free of charge. Instant transfers to a debit card incur a 1.5% fee, subject to a $0.25 minimum. International transfers in the three newly supported markets incur a flat $2.99 fee plus applicable foreign exchange spread, disclosed at the time of transaction.

author: Legal Drafting Team
text:
Consumer Terms and Conditions (CMP-004) | 3.3 Liability for Unauthorized Transactions
Consumers who report an unauthorized transaction within 60 days of the transaction appearing on their account statement will not be held liable for the unauthorized amount, provided the consumer has not shared their account credentials with the unauthorized party. Claims reported after 60 days are reviewed on a case-by-case basis and are not guaranteed reimbursement.

author: Legal Drafting Team
text:
Consumer Terms and Conditions (CMP-004) | 3.4 Account Closure and Fund Access
Veridian Dynamics may close or suspend a consumer account for suspected fraud, sanctions concerns, or violation of these terms. Upon closure, available balances are returned to the consumer's linked bank account within 5 business days, absent an active fraud or sanctions hold.

author: Legal Drafting Team

Consumer Terms and Conditions (CMP-004) | 5. Exceptions, Risks, or Open Issues
The Legal Drafting Team has noted that the 60-day unauthorized transaction reporting window, while generous relative to minimum regulatory expectations, creates potential tension with the Consumer Complaint Resolution Process's 10-business-day final resolution target for unauthorized transaction complaints (CMP-003), since investigations opened near the end of the 60-day window may not always be resolvable within 10 business days if additional documentation is required from banking partners. Legal & Compliance is reviewing whether to adjust either document to better align expectations. The international fee disclosure language is also pending a translated-language accuracy review in the two non-English markets, expected to complete by late 2025.

Deposit Account Training Documentation (DAT-001) | 1. Purpose/Summary
This document describes the training provided to Payment Operations and Customer Success staff who handle deposit account functions, including linked bank account management, ACH origination, hold procedures, and funds availability rules. The training ensures staff understand both the operational mechanics and the regulatory expectations, including Nacha rules referenced in the ACH Compliance Policy (ACH-001), governing deposit-related customer interactions.

author: Prince
text:
Deposit Account Training Documentation (DAT-001) | 2. Background/Context
The training program was introduced in 2025 after Payment Operations identified that front-line Customer Success agents frequently misexplained funds availability timelines to customers, leading to a disproportionate share of fee-dispute and account-access complaints tracked under the Consumer Complaint Resolution Process (CMP-003). Prince partnered with the Customer Success training team to build a joint curriculum covering both the technical deposit account architecture and common customer scenarios, delivered through the ComplianceIQ platform supplemented by live scenario workshops.

author: Prince
text:
Deposit Account Training Documentation (DAT-001) | 3.1 Curriculum Overview
The training consists of a 3-hour core module covering deposit account architecture, linked bank account verification, and standard funds-availability timelines, plus a 1-hour module specific to ACH return handling and customer communication during a return event.

author: Prince
text:
Deposit Account Training Documentation (DAT-001) | 3.2 Funds Availability Rules
Standard ACH-funded deposits become available for platform use within 1 business day of initiation, while instant transfers funded via linked debit card are available immediately upon successful authorization. Staff are trained to explain that funds subject to a fraud or sanctions hold may be delayed regardless of the standard timeline, and must not provide a specific release time estimate to customers in such cases.

author: Prince
text:
Deposit Account Training Documentation (DAT-001) | 3.3 Audience and Completion Requirements
Training is mandatory for all Payment Operations staff and Customer Success agents handling Tier 2 deposit-related escalations (as defined in CMP-003), and is completed within 30 days of role assignment and refreshed annually thereafter.

author: Prince
text:
Deposit Account Training Documentation (DAT-001) | 3.4 Assessment
Staff complete a 15-question knowledge check requiring an 80% passing score, plus a live scenario role-play assessed by a training facilitator for agents handling customer-facing escalations.

text:

author: Prince
text:
Deposit Account Training Documentation (DAT-001) | 5. Exceptions, Risks, or Open Issues
Since the program's 2025 launch, fee-dispute complaints attributable to funds-availability confusion have declined by approximately 22%, though Payment Operations notes this has not been formally validated against a control group and may partly reflect broader complaint-handling improvements under CMP-003. An open item is extending the curriculum to cover the distinct funds-availability rules applicable in the three new international markets, which differ from the domestic 1-business-day standard due to local banking rail processing times; a market-specific addendum is in development with no confirmed release date.

author: Cristiano Ronaldo
text:
Digital Asset Documentation (DIG-001) | 1. Purpose/Summary
This document describes the planned Digital Asset feature for the Veridian Dynamics platform, which would allow consumers to buy, hold, and transfer a limited set of digital assets alongside their existing peer-to-peer payment balance. It outlines the proposed custody model, supported assets, risk considerations, and the cross-functional review process required before any production launch, and is maintained by the product team within Operations in partnership with Legal & Compliance and IT.

author: Cristiano Ronaldo
text:
Digital Asset Documentation (DIG-001) | 2. Background/Context
Cristiano Ronaldo, VP of Product, leads the Digital Asset initiative, which entered a formal feasibility and design phase in mid-2026 following competitive pressure from other peer-to-peer payment providers offering similar functionality. The initiative is explicitly pre-launch: no digital asset functionality is currently live on the platform, and this documentation reflects the design as proposed to the Product Steering Committee, not an operating system. Several other documents in this corpus, including the AML Program Documentation (AML-001), the Risk Management Policy (RSK-001), and the SOC 2 reports, reference the Digital Asset initiative as a forward-looking consideration requiring future control development, underscoring that cross-functional review is still in progress.

author: Cristiano Ronaldo
text:
Digital Asset Documentation (DIG-001) | 3.1 Proposed Custody Model
The current design proposes a custodial model in which Veridian Dynamics, through a licensed third-party custody provider, would hold digital assets on behalf of customers rather than supporting self-custody wallets. This approach is intended to simplify the initial regulatory and security posture relative to a non-custodial design.

author: Cristiano Ronaldo
text:
Digital Asset Documentation (DIG-001) | 3.2 Supported Assets (Proposed)
The initial proposed launch scope includes two widely traded digital assets, selected based on liquidity and regulatory clarity considerations; a final asset list has not been approved and remains subject to Legal & Compliance review of each asset's regulatory classification in relevant jurisdictions.

author: Cristiano Ronaldo
text:
Digital Asset Documentation (DIG-001) | 3.3 Required Cross-Functional Reviews
Before any production launch, the initiative requires: a completed money transmitter licensing analysis per state (led by Legal & Compliance), an AML/CFT control design update incorporating digital asset-specific typologies, a dedicated penetration test of the custody integration (per PEN-001 scope expansion), and a Board Risk Committee approval of the updated risk appetite inclusive of digital asset custody and volatility risk as recommended in the Risk Management Policy (RSK-001).

author: Cristiano Ronaldo
text:
Digital Asset Documentation (DIG-001) | 3.4 Target Timeline
The product team has proposed a target production launch no earlier than Q3 2027, contingent on successful completion of all required cross-functional reviews; this timeline is explicitly preliminary and has not been approved by the Compliance Committee.

author: Cristiano Ronaldo
text:
Digital Asset Documentation (DIG-001) | 4. Key Details
Current production status: Not live; design/feasibility phase
Proposed custody model: Custodial, via licensed third-party provider
Proposed initial supported assets: 2 (final list pending Legal & Compliance review)
Licensing analysis: In progress
AML/CFT control update: Not started
Dedicated penetration test: Not scheduled
Proposed target launch: No earlier than Q3 2027 (preliminary)

author: Cristiano Ronaldo
text:
Digital Asset Documentation (DIG-001) | 5. Exceptions, Risks, or Open Issues
This initiative carries substantial open risk given its early stage: no formal risk taxonomy entry exists yet for digital asset custody and volatility risk, no AML typology coverage has been developed, and licensing analysis across 47 states plus international markets is only partially complete. The product team has emphasized internally that no document in this corpus should be read as describing a live Digital Asset product, and any cross-references to digital assets in other 2026 documentation (such as insurance coverage or penetration testing scope) describe anticipated future needs rather than current controls. The Product Steering Committee has not yet set a formal go/no-go decision date.

author: Lionel Messi
text:
Disaster Recovery Program (DRP-001) | 1. Purpose/Summary
This document defines Veridian Dynamics' Disaster Recovery Program, specifying the technical recovery procedures, infrastructure redundancy, and recovery objectives used to restore the payment processing platform following a significant IT disruption. The program is maintained by IT and is tested through scheduled recovery exercises, with results reported to the Compliance Committee and referenced within the broader Business Continuity Plan (BCP-001).

author: Lionel Messi
text:
Disaster Recovery Program (DRP-001) | 2. Background/Context
The platform is hosted on AWS across two geographically separated regions, with the primary region in US-East and a standby region in US-West configured for active-passive failover. Lionel Messi, Director of Infrastructure, led a program redesign in 2024 following a tabletop exercise that revealed the prior recovery runbook, last updated in 2022, no longer reflected the current microservices architecture or the expanded set of 34 production services now in operation. This version 2.0 reflects updated recovery time and recovery point objectives validated through a full failover test conducted in March 2026, the first full regional failover test the company had performed since migrating to the current architecture.

author: Lionel Messi
text:
Disaster Recovery Program (DRP-001) | 3.1 Recovery Objectives
The program establishes a Recovery Time Objective (RTO) of 8 hours and a Recovery Point Objective (RPO) of 15 minutes for the core transaction processing platform. These objectives were validated during the March 2026 failover test, which achieved a full regional cutover in 7 hours and 12 minutes with data loss measured at 11 minutes, within target.

author: Lionel Messi
text:
Disaster Recovery Program (DRP-001) | 3.2 Infrastructure Redundancy
Database replication between the primary and standby regions uses continuous asynchronous replication with a typical lag of under 2 minutes under normal operating conditions. Standby region capacity is maintained at 100% of production capacity to avoid performance degradation during failover.

author: Lionel Messi
text:
Disaster Recovery Program (DRP-001) | 3.3 Recovery Procedures
Upon declaration of a disaster by the IT Incident Commander, a documented 42-step runbook governs failover, including DNS cutover, database promotion, and service health verification, with each step assigned to a named on-call role rather than a specific individual to ensure coverage regardless of who is on call.

author: Lionel Messi
text:
Disaster Recovery Program (DRP-001) | 3.4 Testing Cadence
Full regional failover tests are conducted annually; tabletop exercises covering partial failure scenarios are conducted quarterly. The next full failover test is scheduled for March 2027.

author: Lionel Messi
text:

Recovery Time Objective (RTO): 8 hours
Recovery Point Objective (RPO): 15 minutes
March 2026 test actual cutover time: 7 hours 12 minutes
March 2026 test actual data loss: 11 minutes
Primary region: AWS US-East
Standby region: AWS US-West
Standby capacity: 100% of production
Full failover test cadence: Annual
Production services in scope: 34

author: Lionel Messi
text:
Disaster Recovery Program (DRP-001) | 5. Exceptions, Risks, or Open Issues
The March 2025 test identified one open issue: three of the 34 production services experienced a delayed health-check registration after failover, adding approximately 25 minutes to the overall cutover time; a remediation item to improve health-check registration speed has been assigned to the platform engineering team with a target completion of Q4 2026. IT has also noted that the 8-hour RTO defined in this program has not yet been reconciled with recovery objectives referenced in the Business Continuity Plan (BCP-001), which covers broader organizational continuity beyond IT systems; a joint review is planned but not yet scheduled.

author: Lebron James
text:
Fraud Program Documentation (FRD-001) | 1. Purpose/Summary
This document establishes the enterprise Fraud Program for Veridian Dynamics' peer-to-peer payment platform. The program defines the governance structure, detection tooling, and response standards used to identify, prevent, and remediate fraudulent activity across consumer and merchant accounts. It applies to all transactions processed through the platform, including person-to-person transfers, linked bank withdrawals, and instant cash-out features. The program is sponsored by the Chief Risk Officer and is reviewed annually by the Fraud Risk Committee to ensure alignment with evolving fraud typologies and regulatory expectations.

author: Lebron James
text:
Fraud Program Documentation (FRD-001) | 2. Background/Context
Veridian Dynamics processes an average of $42 million in daily transaction volume across approximately 3.1 million active user accounts. As transaction volume has grown 35% year-over-year, the fraud landscape has shifted from simple account takeover attempts toward more sophisticated social engineering scams, synthetic identity fraud, and first-party chargeback abuse. In response, the Fraud Operations team, housed within Legal & Compliance, built out a dedicated fraud detection stack in 2023 and has iterated on it through two major version releases. The current program reflects lessons learned from a Q3 2024 fraud spike tied to romance-scam typologies that resulted in elevated consumer complaints and a temporary increase in reserve requirements. The Fraud Risk Committee, composed of representatives from Legal & Compliance, Operations, Finance, and Customer Success, meets monthly to review emerging trends and approve rule changes to the detection engine. This document supersedes the version 1.x program documentation issued in 2023, which lacked formal model governance and relied primarily on manual review queues.

author: Lebron James
text:
Fraud Program Documentation (FRD-001) | 3.1 Detection Infrastructure
The core of the fraud program is SentinelGuard, a proprietary real-time risk scoring engine that evaluates every transaction against more than 120 behavioral and device-fingerprint signals. Transactions scoring above 85 (on a 0-100 risk scale) are automatically held for manual review; transactions scoring above 95 are auto-declined pending customer verification. SentinelGuard is hosted on AWS and integrates with the core ledger system to apply holds within 200 milliseconds of transaction initiation.

author: Lebron James
text:
Fraud Program Documentation (FRD-001) | 3.2 Case Management and Review
Flagged transactions route to the Fraud Operations queue, staffed by 14 full-time analysts across two shifts. Analysts use a standardized decision matrix to determine whether to release, hold pending additional verification, or refer a case for escalation under the Fraud Escalation Process (FRD-002). High-severity cases, defined as confirmed account takeover or losses exceeding $2,500, must be escalated within 24 hours of identification per the escalation SLA defined in this program.

author: Lebron James
text:
Fraud Program Documentation (FRD-001) | 3.3 Loss Thresholds and Reserves
The program targets a monthly net fraud loss rate below 0.08% of total transaction volume. When the rolling 30-day loss rate exceeds this threshold, Fraud Operations must present a remediation plan to the Fraud Risk Committee within five business days. Finance maintains a fraud loss reserve equal to 1.2 times the trailing three-month average loss, adjusted quarterly.

author: Lebron James
text:
Fraud Program Documentation (FRD-001) | 3.4 Customer Communication
Customers whose transactions are held for review receive an in-app notification within 60 seconds, along with a case reference number. Customer Success is granted read-only access to case status (but not underlying risk signals) to support customer inquiries without compromising detection logic.

author: Lebron James
text:
Fraud Program Documentation (FRD-001) | 4. Key Details
Detection engine: SentinelGuard v4.2
Auto-hold risk score threshold: 85 / 100
Auto-decline risk score threshold: 95 / 100
High-severity escalation SLA: 24 hours
High-severity loss threshold: $2,500
Monthly fraud loss target: < 0.08% of volume
Fraud Operations headcount: 14 analysts, 2 shifts
Fraud loss reserve multiplier: 1.2x trailing 3-month average
Governance body: Fraud Risk Committee (monthly)

author: Lebron James
text:
Fraud Program Documentation (FRD-001) | 5. Exceptions, Risks, or Open Issues
An open risk item concerns SentinelGuard's device-fingerprinting coverage on older Android devices, where approximately 6% of sessions cannot be reliably fingerprinted, increasing false-negative risk. A remediation project is scheduled for Q1 2026. Additionally, the Fraud Risk Committee has flagged that romance-scam typologies increasingly involve victims authorizing their own transactions, which existing behavioral models are not optimized to detect, since the account holder themselves is unwittingly complicit. A pilot program using conversational pattern analysis in the in-app chat feature is under evaluation but has not yet been approved for production due to privacy review requirements from Legal & Compliance.

author: Madonna
text:
Fraud Escalation Process (FRD-002) | 1. Purpose/Summary
This document defines the step-by-step process Fraud Operations analysts and Operations leadership follow when escalating confirmed or suspected fraud cases above Tier 1 severity. It specifies escalation paths, notification requirements, and required documentation for each severity tier, and clarifies responsibilities between Fraud Operations, Operations leadership, and Legal & Compliance for cases requiring regulatory reporting or law enforcement referral.

author: Madonna
text:
Fraud Escalation Process (FRD-002) | 2. Background/Context
Following the Fraud Program Documentation (FRD-001) update in late 2024, Operations leadership identified that the prior escalation workflow, which relied on an email distribution list and ad hoc Slack threads, created inconsistent response times and lost audit trails. In Q1 2025, Operations partnered with IT to build a dedicated case management workflow inside the internal ticketing system, giving every escalated case a unique ticket ID, a severity tag, and an automatic timestamp at each stage of review. This version 3.0 of the escalation process reflects operational experience from the first two quarters of use, including feedback that the originally proposed escalation window was difficult for a 14-person analyst team to consistently meet given weekend and holiday staffing gaps. Operations leadership, in consultation with the VP of Risk, revised the escalation window accordingly as part of this release. The process applies platform-wide and is mandatory for all Tier 2 and Tier 3 cases.

author: Madonna
text:
Fraud Escalation Process (FRD-002) | 3.1 Severity Tiers
Cases are classified into three tiers. Tier 1 covers low-dollar, single-account anomalies handled entirely within the standard analyst queue. Tier 2 covers confirmed account takeover, suspected synthetic identity, or losses between $2,500 and $25,000. Tier 3 covers suspected organized fraud rings, losses exceeding $25,000, or any case with potential money laundering nexus requiring coordination with the AML Program.

author: Madonna
text:
Fraud Escalation Process (FRD-002) | 3.2 Escalation Workflow
Upon identifying a Tier 2 or Tier 3 case, the analyst opens an escalation ticket and tags the appropriate severity. Tier 2 cases must be escalated to the Fraud Operations Shift Lead within 48 hours of identification, and the Shift Lead must acknowledge the ticket within 4 business hours of assignment. Tier 3 cases must be escalated immediately to the Operations Director and copied to Legal & Compliance, with a target acknowledgment time of 2 hours.

author: Madonna
text:
Fraud Escalation Process (FRD-002) | 3.3 Documentation Requirements
Every escalated ticket must include the originating transaction ID, risk score at time of flag, a narrative summary, and any supporting evidence such as device fingerprint logs or customer communications. Tickets lacking complete documentation are returned to the originating analyst and do not count toward SLA attainment until resubmitted.

author: Madonna
text:
Fraud Escalation Process (FRD-002) | 3.4 Regulatory and Law Enforcement Referral
Legal & Compliance determines whether a Tier 3 case warrants a Suspicious Activity Report filing or law enforcement referral. This determination must occur within 5 business days of escalation, consistent with the AML Program Documentation (AML-001).

author: Madonna
text:
Fraud Escalation Process (FRD-002) | 4. Key Details
Tier: Tier 1 | Definition: Low-dollar single-account anomaly; Escalation SLA: N/A (queue only); Acknowledgment Target: N/A
Tier: Tier 2 | Definition: Account takeover / $2,500-$25,000 loss; Escalation SLA: 48 hours; Acknowledgment Target: 4 business hours
Tier: Tier 3 | Definition: Organized fraud / >$25,000 / AML nexus; Escalation SLA: Immediate; Acknowledgment Target: 2 hours

author: Madonna
text:
Fraud Escalation Process (FRD-002) | 5. Exceptions, Risks, or Open Issues
Operations leadership has acknowledged that the revised 48-hour Tier 2 escalation window, while more achievable for current staffing levels, has not yet been formally reconciled with the 24-hour high-severity SLA referenced in the Fraud Program Documentation (FRD-001). A joint review between Operations and Legal & Compliance is tentatively scheduled for the next Fraud Risk Committee meeting to align the two documents. In the interim, analysts have been instructed to follow the 48-hour window specified in this process document. A secondary open issue involves weekend coverage: Tier 3 cases identified between Friday 8:00 PM and Monday 6:00 AM currently route to an on-call rotation that has experienced two missed-acknowledgment incidents since March 2025.

author: David Beckham
text:
Insurance Coverage Policy (INS-001) | 1. Purpose/Summary
This document summarizes the corporate insurance coverage maintained by Veridian Dynamics to manage residual financial risk from operational losses, cyber incidents, directors' and officers' liability, and crime-related exposures. It is maintained by Finance in coordination with Enterprise Risk Management and is reviewed annually ahead of policy renewal to ensure coverage levels remain aligned with the company's growth and risk profile.

author: David Beckham
text:
Insurance Coverage Policy (INS-001) | 2. Background/Context
David Beckham, VP of Finance, manages the insurance program through a broker relationship with a national commercial insurance brokerage. Coverage levels have been increased twice in the past two years to keep pace with transaction volume growth and the company's expanded regulatory footprint across 47 states and three new international markets. The most recent renewal, effective June 1, 2026, included a notable increase in cyber liability coverage following broker and underwriter guidance that reflected rising claims costs industry-wide for payment processing companies, as well as the company's own loss experience, which has been favorable with no material claims filed in the past three policy years.

author: David Beckham
text:
Insurance Coverage Policy (INS-001) | 3.1 Cyber Liability Coverage
The cyber liability policy provides $25 million in aggregate coverage, up from $15 million in the prior policy year, covering data breach response costs, business interruption from cyber incidents, regulatory fines and penalties where insurable, and third-party liability claims. The policy carries a $500,000 per-incident deductible.

author: David Beckham
text:
Insurance Coverage Policy (INS-001) | 3.2 Crime and Fidelity Coverage
A crime and fidelity bond provides $10 million in coverage for employee theft, funds transfer fraud, and computer fraud, with a $100,000 deductible. This coverage is required under several of the company's state money transmitter licenses, which mandate minimum fidelity bond coverage tied to transaction volume.

author: David Beckham
text:
Insurance Coverage Policy (INS-001) | 3.3 Directors' and Officers' Liability
D&O; coverage provides $20 million in aggregate protection for claims against company directors and officers arising from alleged mismanagement, regulatory actions, or breach of fiduciary duty, with separate Side A coverage ensuring individual director protection even if the company is unable to indemnify.

author: David Beckham
text:
Insurance Coverage Policy (INS-001) | 3.4 Errors and Omissions
A $15 million errors and omissions policy covers claims arising from alleged negligence in the design or operation of the payment platform, including processing errors affecting customer funds.

author: David Beckham
text:
Insurance Coverage Policy (INS-001) | 4. Key Details
Coverage Type: Cyber liability | Limit: $25 million aggregate; Deductible: $500,000 per incident
Coverage Type: Crime and fidelity bond | Limit: $10 million; Deductible: $100,000
Coverage Type: Directors' and officers' liability | Limit: $20 million aggregate; Deductible: Varies by claim type
Coverage Type: Errors and omissions | Limit: $15 million; Deductible: $250,000 per claim

author: David Beckham
text:
Insurance Coverage Policy (INS-001) | 5. Exceptions, Risks, or Open Issues
Finance has flagged that the current $10 million crime and fidelity bond, while compliant with the minimum requirements of all 47 state licenses individually, may be insufficient relative to the aggregate fraud loss exposure implied by the 0.15% operational loss tolerance threshold set in the Risk Management Policy (RSK-001) at current transaction volumes; a coverage adequacy analysis has been commissioned ahead of the next renewal cycle. Cyber liability coverage does not currently extend to claims arising from the planned Digital Asset product line, which the broker has indicated would require a separate rider once that product's risk profile and transaction volume are better defined.

author: David Beckham
text:

ISO 27001 Certification (ISO-001) | 1. Purpose/Summary
This document records Veridian Dynamics' ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification, issued by Meridian Standards Registrar following a successful Stage 1 and Stage 2 audit of the company's Information Security Management System (ISMS). The certification confirms that the ISMS, covering the scope of the production payment processing environment and supporting corporate IT functions, conforms to the ISO 27001 standard's requirements for establishing, implementing, maintaining, and continually improving information security.

author: Certification Body (Meridian Standards Registrar)
text:
ISO 27001 Certification (ISO-001) | 2. Background/Context
Veridian Dynamics began its ISO 27001 certification journey in 2025 as part of a broader strategy to support expansion into international markets where ISO 27001 certification is a common procurement requirement for payment service providers. The IT department, in partnership with an external ISMS consultant, conducted a gap assessment against the standard's Annex A controls in early 2025, implemented remediation across 18 identified gaps throughout the year, and underwent Stage 1 documentation review in November 2025 followed by Stage 2 on-site audit in February 2026. The certification scope explicitly includes the AWS-hosted production environment, the corporate office network in Gotham City, and the software development lifecycle, but excludes certain back-office HR systems managed entirely within PeopleHub, which are addressed under a separate internal control framework.

author: Certification Body (Meridian Standards Registrar)

Of the 93 Annex A controls in ISO/IEC 27001:2022, 87 were determined applicable to Veridian Dynamics' ISMS scope; 6 were excluded with documented justification, primarily related to physical media handling controls not applicable to the company's cloud-native infrastructure.

author: Certification Body (Meridian Standards Registrar)

The Stage 2 audit identified 2 minor nonconformities related to incomplete documentation of supplier security review records and inconsistent application of the asset inventory tagging standard. author: Thierry Henry
text:
Information Security Policy (ISP-001) | 1. Purpose/Summary
This Information Security Policy establishes the baseline security requirements for all systems, data, and personnel at Veridian Dynamics. It covers access control, data classification and encryption, network security, vulnerability management, and acceptable use, and serves as the primary internal policy document underlying the company's ISO 27001 certification (ISO-001) and SOC 2 examinations (SOC-003, SOC-004).

author: Thierry Henry
text:
Information Security Policy (ISP-001) | 2. Background/Context
The Information Security Policy has been revised four times since its initial 2021 adoption, with this version 4.0 representing a substantial rewrite undertaken in 2026 specifically to prepare for the ISO 27001 certification project. Wendell Park, who holds dual responsibility for IT Training and security policy documentation, restructured the policy to explicitly map each control statement to the relevant ISO 27001 Annex A reference, replacing the prior narrative-style policy that auditors had found difficult to cross-reference during the SOC 2 Type I examination. The policy applies to all employees, contractors, and third-party service providers with access to Veridian Dynamics systems or data.

author: Thierry Henry
text:
Information Security Policy (ISP-001) | 3.1 Access Control
All production system access requires multi-factor authentication and is granted according to the principle of least privilege through role-based access control. Access reviews are conducted quarterly for standard roles and monthly for privileged administrative roles. Access must be revoked within 24 hours of employee termination or role change.

author: Thierry Henry
text:
Information Security Policy (ISP-001) | 3.2 Data Classification and Encryption
Data is classified into four tiers: Public, Internal, Confidential, and Restricted. Restricted data, including customer financial account details and authentication credentials, must be encrypted at rest using AES-256 and in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher. Confidential data follows the same encryption standards with relaxed access logging requirements relative to Restricted data.

author: Thierry Henry
text:
Information Security Policy (ISP-001) | 3.3 Vulnerability Management
Critical vulnerabilities identified through automated scanning must be remediated within 7 days of identification; high-severity vulnerabilities within 30 days; medium-severity within 90 days. Vulnerability scanning runs continuously against production infrastructure, supplemented by the periodic penetration testing described in the Penetration Testing Procedure (PEN-001).

author: Thierry Henry
text:
Information Security Policy (ISP-001) | 3.4 Acceptable Use and Incident Reporting
All personnel must report suspected security incidents to the IT Security team within 1 hour of discovery through the dedicated incident reporting channel. Use of unapproved third-party cloud storage or AI tools for handling Confidential or Restricted data is prohibited absent explicit IT Security approval.

author: Thierry Henry
text:

Incident reporting window: 1 hour of discovery

author: Thierry Henry
text:
Information Security Policy (ISP-001) | 5. Exceptions, Risks, or Open Issues
IT has identified that the current monthly privileged-access review cadence, while meeting the policy's stated requirement, has experienced two instances of delayed completion in 2026 due to reviewer availability during the ISO 27001 certification project crunch period; both reviews were completed within an additional 5 business days of the deadline, which IT has internally flagged as a minor control gap for tracking purposes even though it fell short of triggering a formal nonconformity. The policy's prohibition on unapproved AI tool use for Confidential or Restricted data is under active review as several business teams have requested expanded, approved use cases, and a formal AI tool approval process is being drafted jointly by IT and Legal & Compliance.

IT Training Documentation (ITT-001) | 1. Purpose/Summary
This document describes the training curriculum required for IT department staff at Veridian Dynamics, covering secure coding practices, cloud infrastructure management, incident response procedures, and change management discipline. The training program supplements the general Compliance Training Documentation (CMP-001) with technical depth appropriate to engineering and infrastructure roles, and is administered by the IT Training Lead under the VP of Infrastructure.

author: Thierry Henry
text:
IT Training Documentation (ITT-001) | 2. Background/Context
Wendell Park, IT Training Lead, developed the current curriculum in 2024 in response to findings from an internal security review that identified inconsistent secure coding practices across engineering teams, particularly around input validation and credential handling in newly written services. The curriculum was also shaped by requirements emerging from the ISO 27001 certification project (ISO-001), which required documented evidence of role-specific security training for personnel with access to production systems. This version 1.5 update added a dedicated module on incident response procedures following the Disaster Recovery Program's (DRP-001) 2026 failover test, which revealed that several engineers were unfamiliar with their assigned on-call runbook roles.

author: Thierry Henry
text:
IT Training Documentation (ITT-001) | 3.1 Curriculum Modules
All engineering and infrastructure staff complete four mandatory modules: secure coding fundamentals (3 hours), cloud infrastructure security (2 hours), incident response and on-call readiness (2 hours), and change management and deployment discipline (1 hour), for a total of 8 hours annually.

author: Thierry Henry
text:
IT Training Documentation (ITT-001) | 3.2 Role-Based Additions
Engineers with production database access complete an additional 2-hour data handling and encryption module. Engineers assigned to the on-call rotation complete a hands-on incident response simulation exercise twice per year in addition to the standard module.

author: Thierry Henry
text:
IT Training Documentation (ITT-001) | 3.3 Delivery and Assessment
Training is delivered through a combination of the ComplianceIQ platform for conceptual modules and live hands-on workshops for the incident response simulation. Conceptual modules require an 85% passing score on a knowledge check; the incident response simulation is assessed through facilitator observation against a documented readiness checklist rather than a written test.

author: Thierry Henry
text:
IT Training Documentation (ITT-001) | 3.4 Completion Tracking
IT Training completion is tracked separately from general Compliance Training and reported to the VP of Infrastructure quarterly, with results also shared with Legal & Compliance to support ISO 27001 surveillance audit evidence requests.

The March 2025 failover test finding regarding on-call runbook unfamiliarity has prompted a proposal to increase the incident response simulation frequency from twice to three times per year for 2027, pending budget and scheduling approval from the VP of Infrastructure. IT Training has also identified a gap in current curriculum coverage of the AWS services planned for the Digital Asset product line, including key management service usage patterns specific to that product; a new module is in development with no confirmed completion date. Completion tracking for contractors and contingent IT staff remains manual and is not yet integrated into the quarterly reporting process.

text:
Onboarding Training Documentation (ONB-001) | 1. Purpose/Summary
This document describes the new-hire onboarding training curriculum delivered to all Veridian Dynamics employees during their first 30 days of employment, covering company policies, systems access, code of conduct, and an introduction to the compliance obligations relevant to a payment services company. It is administered by HR through the PeopleHub platform and is distinct from, but feeds into, the ongoing annual Compliance Training Documentation (CMP-001).

author: Jalen Brunson
text:
Onboarding Training Documentation (ONB-001) | 2. Background/Context
Jalen Brunson, VP of People Operations, oversees the onboarding program, which was redesigned in 2024 to reduce new-hire time-to-productivity following an internal survey indicating that new hires found the prior fully asynchronous onboarding confusing and difficult to complete alongside their initial job responsibilities. The redesigned program introduced a structured cohort model, grouping new hires who start within the same two-week window into a shared onboarding cohort with live orientation sessions supplementing the asynchronous PeopleHub modules. This version 1.4 update added a dedicated compliance-foundations session following feedback from Legal & Compliance that new hires in customer-facing or transaction-handling roles were starting their jobs before receiving any compliance context, relying entirely on the annual training cycle which could be up to 11 months away depending on start date.

author: Jalen Brunson
text:
Onboarding Training Documentation (ONB-001) | 3.1 Onboarding Structure
New hires complete a 2-day live orientation covering company history, organizational structure, benefits enrollment, and systems setup, followed by role-specific asynchronous modules in PeopleHub to be completed within the first 30 days. All new hires are assigned to a cohort based on start date.

author: Jalen Brunson
text:
Onboarding Training Documentation (ONB-001) | 3.2 Compliance Foundations Session
All new hires complete a 1-hour Compliance Foundations session during orientation week, delivered live by a member of the Legal & Compliance training team, covering the company's regulatory status as a money services business, the basic concept of suspicious activity, and where to direct compliance questions. This session is in addition to, not a replacement for, the full annual Compliance Training (CMP-001), which new hires complete within 30 days of their start date per that document's new-hire provision.

author: Jalen Brunson
text:
Onboarding Training Documentation (ONB-001) | 3.3 Role-Specific Onboarding Tracks
Beyond the shared orientation, onboarding branches into role-specific tracks: an engineering track including development environment setup and the relevant portions of IT Training (ITT-001), a Customer Success track including support tooling and complaint-handling basics, and a general corporate track for other roles.

author: Jalen Brunson
text:
Onboarding Training Documentation (ONB-001) | 3.4 Completion Tracking
HR tracks onboarding completion through PeopleHub, with managers receiving a completion summary at the 30-day mark and a formal check-in meeting scheduled at 30, 60, and 90 days to assess onboarding effectiveness and address any gaps.

author: Jalen Brunson
text:
Onboarding Training Documentation (ONB-001) | 5. Exceptions, Risks, or Open Issues
HR has noted that the Compliance Foundations session, while well-received in post-orientation surveys, is currently delivered only in English, which creates a gap for new hires joining the three new international market offices who may prefer local-language delivery; a translated version is under development with Legal & Compliance but not yet available. Additionally, the cohort model occasionally creates a delay for new hires who start outside a standard cohort window (for example, due to a delayed start date), who may wait up to 10 additional days for their live orientation session; HR is evaluating whether to add a smaller supplemental cohort session to reduce this gap.

text:
Penetration Testing Procedure (PEN-001) | 1. Purpose/Summary
This procedure defines how Veridian Dynamics plans, executes, and remediates findings from penetration testing of its production payment platform and supporting infrastructure. It specifies testing scope, cadence, engagement of qualified third-party testers, and remediation timelines, and operationalizes the vulnerability management requirements of the Information Security Policy (ISP-001).

author: Karim Benzema
text:
Penetration Testing Procedure (PEN-001) | 2. Background/Context
Karim Benzema, Security Engineering Manager, oversees the penetration testing program, which engages an independent third-party testing firm, Ironclad Security Labs, rather than relying solely on internal red-team exercises, in order to provide independent assurance to enterprise partners and support SOC 2 examination evidence requirements. The current version reflects an expanded testing scope added in 2025 to include the newly launched international payment corridors and the AWS infrastructure supporting the three new markets entered in Q2 2026. Testing was previously limited to the core domestic platform.

author: Karim Benzema
text:
Penetration Testing Procedure (PEN-001) | 3.1 Testing Scope and Cadence
Full-scope external and internal network penetration testing is conducted semi-annually. Application-layer penetration testing of the core payment platform, including API endpoints and mobile application backends, is conducted quarterly. Ad hoc testing is triggered for any major architecture change, such as the international expansion rollout.

author: Karim Benzema
text:
Penetration Testing Procedure (PEN-001) | 3.2 Engagement Process
Ironclad Security Labs operates under a signed rules-of-engagement document defining testing windows, excluded systems, and emergency stop procedures. Testing is conducted against a staging environment that mirrors production configuration wherever possible to avoid customer-facing disruption, with limited production testing windows for specific checks that cannot be validated in staging.

author: Karim Benzema
text:
Penetration Testing Procedure (PEN-001) | 3.3 Finding Classification and Remediation
Findings are classified using a CVSS-based severity scale. Critical findings (CVSS 9.0+) require remediation within 7 days and immediate notification to the VP of Infrastructure. High findings (CVSS 7.0-8.9) require remediation within 30 days. Medium and low findings are tracked in the standard vulnerability backlog per the Information Security Policy's (ISP-001) general remediation SLAs.

author: Karim Benzema
text:
Penetration Testing Procedure (PEN-001) | 3.4 Reporting
A full findings report is delivered by Ironclad Security Labs within 10 business days of test completion, with an executive summary presented to the Compliance Committee. A retest of all critical and high findings is conducted within 45 days of the original report to confirm remediation.

author: Karim Benzema
text:

author: Karim Benzema
